14 A beam QR is held in position by a wire PQ. The structure is used to form a crane supporting a
stationary load of 4.0 kN, as shown.
P
Q
30
vertical
wall
R
4.0 kN
What is the force exerted by the beam QR on point Q?
A
4.0 kN
B
4.6 kN
C
6.9 kN
D
8.0 kN

hints: Notice point Q is in equilibrium with three forces: the $4.0 \text{ kN}$ weight down, the horizontal pull of wire PQ to the left, and the push of beam QR.
The beam QR makes $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal wire PQ, so resolve the beam force $F$ into vertical $F \sin 30^{\circ}$ and horizontal $F \cos 30^{\circ}$ components.
Set upward forces equal to downward forces at Q: $F \sin 30^{\circ} = 4.0 \text{ kN}$, then solve for $F$ using $\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5$.
walkthrough: Identify forces at Q: $4.0 \text{ kN}$ vertically down from the load, tension $T$ in wire PQ horizontally to the left, and force $F$ from beam QR acting along the beam.
Because the beam is a strut in compression, it pushes Q away from R. From the diagram R is down and left of Q, so the push on Q is up and right at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal.
For equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so resolve vertically: upward component from beam must equal downward load. That is $F \sin 30^{\circ} = 4.0 \text{ kN}$.
Solve: $F = 4.0 / 0.5 = 8.0 \text{ kN}$. Units remain $\text{kN}$ and the beam is in compression. This is option D.

A.explanation: 4.0 kN is only the vertical load. It ignores that the beam acts at $30^{\circ}$ so only part of its force is vertical.

B.explanation: 4.6 kN comes from using $4.0 / \cos 30^{\circ}$. The $4.0 \text{ kN}$ load must balance the vertical component with $\sin 30^{\circ}$, not $\cos 30^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: 6.9 kN is the tension in the horizontal wire PQ, found from $4.0 / \tan 30^{\circ}$. It is not the force along the beam QR.

D.explanation: The vertical component $F \sin 30^{\circ}$ of the beam force balances the $4.0 \text{ kN}$ load, giving $F = 8.0 \text{ kN}$ in compression.
